checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for EDGE-RPC-CALL: JSON-RPC input validation
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Send malformed JSON-RPC requests to eth_config and eth_sendRawTransaction endpoints. 2. Submit requests with invalid method names, missing required fields, and oversized payloads. 3. Verify the node rejects all malformed inputs with appropriate error codes. 4. Test type coercion attacks (numeric strings where integers expected). 5. Confirm rate limiting is enforced for eth_config (recommended 1s interval per trust model).
executable_checks: fuzzing: JSON-RPC endpoint with malformed payloads
static_analysis: input validation at RPC handler entry points
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-EIP7927-PRECOND-003. Trust edge EDGE-RPC-CALL from EXT-USER-JSON-RPC to EL JSON-RPC interface. Security assumption requires full request validation, rate limiting, and access restriction.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for EDGE-EVM-UNTRUSTED-CALL: EVM call data format validation
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Craft EVM transactions with malformed call data targeting CALL/STATICCALL/DELEGATECALL opcodes. 2. Test precompile inputs with invalid point-on-curve data and incorrect input lengths (EIP-1108). 3. Verify STATICCALL enforces read-only: attempt CREATE, LOG, SSTORE, SELFDESTRUCT, CALL-with-value within STATICCALL context. 4. Test STATIC flag propagation through nested calls. 5. Test EIP-7702 delegation resolution does not exceed one level.
executable_checks: fuzzing: EVM call data with malformed inputs
unit_test: STATICCALL enforcement with prohibited opcodes
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-EIP5-PRECOND-015. Trust edge EDGE-EVM-UNTRUSTED-CALL from EXT-UNTRUSTED-CONTRACT-EVM to EL EVM execution. Security assumption covers STATICCALL read-only enforcement and precompile input validation.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for EDGE-PEER-BLOCK-FORK: block size limit enforcement at fork boundary
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Submit blocks with payloads exceeding expected size limits at the fork transition boundary. 2. Test block validation with block numbers at, just below, and just above the Berlin activation threshold. 3. Verify the correct rule set (pre-Berlin vs post-Berlin) is applied based on block number. 4. Send oversized block headers and bodies to confirm resource exhaustion prevention. 5. Confirm nodes disconnect peers submitting invalid oversized blocks.
executable_checks: integration_test: oversized block rejection at fork boundary
unit_test: fork rule selection based on block number
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-EIP606-PRECOND-063. Trust edge EDGE-PEER-BLOCK-FORK from EXT-PEER-NODE-BLOCKS to EL block validation. Security assumption requires block number check against fork activation threshold.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for EDGE-TYPE4-TX-SUBMIT: Type-4 transaction format validation
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Submit Type-4 transactions with empty authorization lists and verify rejection. 2. Submit Type-4 transactions with null destination and verify rejection. 3. Test authorization tuples: invalid chain_id (not 0 or current), nonce >= 2^64-1, invalid ecrecover signatures, s > secp256k1n/2. 4. Verify sender must be EOA or delegated account. 5. Test authority code validation: must be empty or existing delegation. 6. Verify authority nonce matching.
executable_checks: unit_test: Type-4 transaction validation rules
fuzzing: authorization tuple fields with boundary values
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-EIP7702-PRECOND-027. Trust edge EDGE-TYPE4-TX-SUBMIT from EXT-TX-SUBMITTER-TYPE4 to EL transaction pool. Security assumption covers comprehensive Type-4 validation rules.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for EDGE-RECEIVE-ATTESTATION: attestation cryptographic validity
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Submit attestations with invalid BLS signatures and verify rejection. 2. Submit attestations outside the extended gossip window (beyond epoch N+1) and verify they are dropped. 3. Test with stale attestations from old epochs. 4. Submit attestations with valid format but tampered data fields and verify signature check catches them. 5. Flood attestation gossip channel and verify rate limiting prevents resource exhaustion.
executable_checks: unit_test: BLS signature verification for attestations
integration_test: gossip window enforcement
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-CAPELLA-VAL-PRECOND-004. Trust edge EDGE-RECEIVE-ATTESTATION from EXT-GOSSIP-PEER-P2P to CL attestation validation. Security assumption requires extended gossip window check and rate limiting.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for EDGE-EVM-UNTRUSTED-CALL: EVM call input size limits for EIP-8024 extended stack
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Execute EVM calls with extremely deep stack usage targeting extended stack access opcodes. 2. Test call data payloads at and beyond size limits. 3. Verify gas metering correctly accounts for extended stack operations. 4. Test nested calls with maximum stack depth to confirm no out-of-bounds memory access. 5. Verify STATICCALL restrictions hold under extended stack operations.
executable_checks: unit_test: gas metering for extended stack opcodes
fuzzing: call data size at boundary limits
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-EIP8024-PRECOND-071. Trust edge EDGE-EVM-UNTRUSTED-CALL. Focus on resource exhaustion via extended stack depth operations.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for EDGE-BLOCK-PROPOSER-INCLUSION: beacon block attestation inclusion size limits
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Propose beacon blocks with an excessive number of attestations exceeding expected limits. 2. Test blocks with attestations that have oversized aggregation bitfields. 3. Verify all included attestations are within the extended inclusion window (EIP-7045). 4. Submit blocks with attestations just outside the inclusion window and verify rejection. 5. Confirm TIMELY_TARGET_FLAG handling for valid attestations without inclusion_delay constraint.
executable_checks: integration_test: beacon block with oversized attestation payload
unit_test: EIP-7045 inclusion window validation
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-ELECTRA-PRECOND-099. Trust edge EDGE-BLOCK-PROPOSER-INCLUSION from EXT-BLOCK-PROPOSER-P2P to CL beacon block validation.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for EDGE-EVM-UNTRUSTED-CALL: cryptographic validity of inputs for transient storage operations
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Execute TSTORE/TLOAD operations through untrusted CALL/DELEGATECALL and verify transient storage isolation per transaction. 2. Test precompile calls with invalid elliptic curve points and verify rejection. 3. Verify STATICCALL context prevents TSTORE writes. 4. Test DELEGATECALL transient storage scope to confirm it operates on caller's transient storage, not callee's. 5. Verify input length validation for precompile contracts.
executable_checks: unit_test: transient storage isolation through call types
unit_test: precompile input validation
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-PRAGUE-STORAGE-PRECOND-048. Trust edge EDGE-EVM-UNTRUSTED-CALL. Focus on cryptographic input validity for storage-related operations.

checklist.title: Falsify ambiguity resolution: alternate block data validation interpretations produce divergent outcomes
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Identify the validation requirements for block data from alternate sources in each major client implementation. 2. Compare validation logic across at least two clients (e.g., Geth, Nethermind). 3. Construct block data that passes validation in one client but fails in another due to ambiguous validation requirements. 4. If such divergence exists, document the specific validation difference.
executable_checks: cross_client_test: block data validation from alternate sources
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-EIP7927-INV-007. Ambiguity AMB-EIP7927-03. Invariant type: attempt to show two valid interpretations produce different behavior.

checklist.title: Falsify assumption: applications fail catastrophically when historical data is unavailable
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Simulate data unavailability by making historical block data inaccessible post-EIP-7927. 2. Run common dApp operations (token transfers, DEX swaps, NFT mints) that may depend on historical data. 3. Verify whether applications handle unavailability gracefully or crash/produce incorrect results. 4. Check if alternate data source fallback mechanisms exist in tooling.
executable_checks: integration_test: dApp behavior under historical data unavailability
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-EIP7927-PRECOND-011. Assumption ASSUM-EIP7927-04. Pre-condition: attempt to show applications do NOT handle data unavailability gracefully.

checklist.title: Falsify assumption: called contract can corrupt memory outside designated output area
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Deploy a contract that writes extensively to memory during a CALL. 2. From the calling contract, specify output_start and output_size that bound a specific memory region. 3. After the CALL returns, read memory regions outside the designated output area. 4. Verify the caller's memory outside [output_start, output_start+output_size] is unmodified. 5. Test with output_size=0 and verify no memory corruption occurs.
executable_checks: unit_test: EVM CALL output bounds enforcement
fuzzing: output_start and output_size edge cases
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-EIP5-PRECOND-019. Assumption ASSUM-EIP5-01. Pre-condition: attempt to bypass output bounds enforcement.

checklist.title: Falsify pre-condition: output_start + output_size causes integer overflow in memory expansion gas
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Craft a CALL with output_start = 2^256 - 1 and output_size = 1 to trigger potential overflow. 2. Test with output_start = 0 and output_size = 2^256 - 1. 3. Test with both values set to 2^128 (product overflows 256 bits). 4. Verify the EVM either reverts with out-of-gas or correctly computes memory expansion cost without overflow. 5. Compare behavior across client implementations.
executable_checks: unit_test: integer overflow in memory expansion gas calculation
cross_client_test: overflow handling consistency
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-EIP5-PRECOND-023. Primary element SPEC-EIP5. Pre-condition: attempt to cause integer overflow via output parameters.

checklist.title: Falsify ambiguity resolution: 'permanently set code' vs clearing delegation with address 0x0 produces inconsistent state
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Set delegation for an EOA to a contract address via Type-4 transaction. 2. Clear delegation by setting address to 0x0. 3. Verify account behaves as standard EOA after clearing. 4. Compare state across clients: check if any client retains residual delegation state. 5. Set delegation again after clearing and verify clean state transition.
executable_checks: cross_client_test: delegation set/clear/re-set cycle consistency
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-EIP7702-INV-031. Ambiguity AMB-EIP7702-01. Invariant: attempt to show 'permanent' and 'clearable' interpretations diverge.

checklist.title: Falsify post-condition: account retains code behavior after delegation cleared to 0x0
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Create EOA, set delegation to a contract with storage-writing logic. 2. Execute transactions using the delegated code. 3. Clear delegation by setting address to 0x0. 4. Attempt to call the account and verify it behaves as a codeless EOA (no code execution). 5. Verify EXTCODESIZE, EXTCODEHASH return values consistent with empty code. 6. Check that any storage written during delegation persists but is inaccessible via code.
executable_checks: unit_test: account behavior after delegation clearing
integration_test: EXTCODESIZE/EXTCODEHASH after clearing
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-EIP7702-POSTCOND-043. Primary element SPEC-EIP7702. Post-condition: verify no residual code behavior after clearing.

checklist.title: Falsify assumption: users sign authorization tuples without understanding code execution rights
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Review wallet UIs (MetaMask, etc.) for how Type-4 authorization tuple signing is presented. 2. Construct a misleading dApp that requests authorization tuple signing with an obfuscated delegation target. 3. Assess whether standard wallet warnings adequately convey that code execution rights are being granted. 4. Test if a user can be tricked into signing authorization to a malicious contract.
executable_checks: manual_review: wallet UI for Type-4 authorization display
integration_test: dApp authorization request flow
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-EIP7702-PRECOND-035. Assumption ASSUM-EIP7702-01. Pre-condition: attempt to show users do NOT understand what they are signing.

checklist.title: Falsify assumption: 0xef0100 prefix conflicts with future EVM features or EOF
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Review EOF (EIP-3540, EIP-7692) magic byte sequences and verify no overlap with 0xef0100. 2. Check all reserved EVM prefix ranges in current and proposed EIPs. 3. Attempt to deploy a contract with code starting with 0xef0100 and verify it is treated as delegation marker, not executable code. 4. Verify EXTCODECOPY of a delegated account returns the delegation prefix correctly.
executable_checks: static_analysis: EVM prefix namespace allocation
unit_test: 0xef0100 prefix handling
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-EIP7702-PRECOND-039. Assumption ASSUM-EIP7702-05. Pre-condition: attempt to find namespace collision with 0xef0100.

checklist.title: Falsify ambiguity resolution: cross-layer EIP classification produces divergent layer assignments
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Identify EIPs that span multiple layers (e.g., EIP-7702 touches networking and execution). 2. Check how different EIP editors and clients classify these cross-layer EIPs. 3. Determine if ambiguous classification affects implementation scope or testing coverage. 4. Document any EIP where layer classification disagreement could lead to incomplete implementation.
executable_checks: manual_review: cross-layer EIP classification consistency
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-EIP4-INV-047. Ambiguity AMB-EIP4-01. Invariant: attempt to show layer boundary ambiguity causes practical problems.

checklist.title: Falsify invariant: an EIP is classified into multiple layers simultaneously
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Query the EIP repository for all EIPs and their layer classifications. 2. Check for any EIP assigned to more than one layer. 3. Check for any EIP with no layer assignment. 4. If duplicates found, verify whether this causes implementation or governance issues.
executable_checks: static_analysis: EIP metadata layer field uniqueness check
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-EIP4-INV-051. Primary element SPEC-EIP4. Invariant: attempt to find an EIP violating single-layer classification.

checklist.title: Falsify ambiguity resolution: disconnect reason codes differ across clients for forkid mismatch
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Connect to nodes running different client implementations (Geth, Nethermind, Besu, Erigon). 2. Send an incompatible forkid during eth/64 handshake. 3. Capture the disconnect reason code from each client. 4. Compare reason codes: if they differ, the ambiguity is unresolved. 5. Assess if differing disconnect codes cause interoperability issues (e.g., reconnection logic).
executable_checks: integration_test: disconnect reason code comparison across clients
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-EIP2364-INV-055. Ambiguity AMB-EIP2364-02. Invariant: attempt to show clients use different disconnect reason codes.

checklist.title: Falsify pre-condition: node accepts connection despite incompatible forkid
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Connect to a node using eth/64 protocol with a forkid from an incompatible fork. 2. Verify the node disconnects immediately. 3. Test with a forkid that is valid but for a future fork not yet activated. 4. Test with a forkid containing correct fork hash but wrong next-fork value. 5. Verify no messages are processed after an incompatible forkid is detected.
executable_checks: integration_test: forkid validation during eth/64 handshake
unit_test: forkid comparison logic
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-EIP2364-PRECOND-059. Primary element SPEC-EIP2364. Pre-condition: attempt to bypass forkid check.

checklist.title: Falsify assumption: activation block number did not provide adequate coordination time
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Review historical data for the Homestead fork activation. 2. Check what percentage of nodes had upgraded by the activation block. 3. Identify any chain splits or orphaned blocks around the activation block. 4. If evidence of inadequate coordination exists, document the impact.
executable_checks: manual_review: historical fork activation data
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-EIP606-PRECOND-067. Assumption ASSUM-EIP606-02. Pre-condition: attempt to show coordination time was insufficient.

checklist.title: Falsify ambiguity resolution: domain separator field ordering produces different hashes
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Construct an EIP-712 domain separator with fields in the canonical order. 2. Construct the same domain separator with fields in a different order. 3. Compute the EIP-712 hash for both orderings in multiple libraries (ethers.js, web3.py, viem). 4. If hashes differ, signatures become non-portable across libraries. 5. Test wallet implementations: do they enforce 'must appear in order' or accept 'any order'?
executable_checks: unit_test: EIP-712 hash with reordered domain separator fields
cross_library_test: hash consistency
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-EIP712-INV-083. Ambiguity AMB-EIP712-02. Invariant: attempt to show field ordering ambiguity produces hash divergence.

checklist.title: Falsify invariant: two structurally different EIP-712 messages produce the same hash
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Construct two EIP-712 messages with different type structures but similar data. 2. Test with nested structs that flatten to similar byte sequences. 3. Test with dynamic types (bytes, string) that could produce colliding encodings. 4. Verify the typeHash differentiation prevents structural collisions. 5. Test with empty arrays vs missing fields.
executable_checks: unit_test: EIP-712 hash collision resistance across type structures
fuzzing: structural variations
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-EIP712-INV-091. Primary element SPEC-EIP712. Invariant: attempt to find a hash collision between structurally different messages.

checklist.title: Falsify post-condition: EIP-712 hash computation is non-deterministic
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Compute the EIP-712 hash for the same message 1000 times and verify all results are identical. 2. Compute across different platforms (x86, ARM) and verify consistency. 3. Test with messages containing maximum-length fields to check for truncation differences. 4. Verify determinism when domain separator contains optional fields.
executable_checks: unit_test: hash determinism across repeated computations
cross_platform_test: hash consistency
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-EIP712-POSTCOND-095. Primary element SPEC-EIP712. Post-condition: attempt to produce different hashes from identical inputs.

checklist.title: Falsify assumption: attacker constructs different typed data producing the same hash
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Analyze EIP-712 encoding for potential second-preimage attacks. 2. Test if a different type structure can produce the same typeHash via hash collision. 3. Test if manipulating dynamic type lengths can produce colliding encodedData. 4. Verify the 0x1901 prefix and domain separator prevent cross-domain replay. 5. Assess computational feasibility of finding collisions given keccak256 security.
executable_checks: cryptographic_analysis: EIP-712 second-preimage resistance
unit_test: cross-type hash independence
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-EIP712-PRECOND-087. Assumption ASSUM-EIP712-02. Pre-condition: attempt to construct a collision.

checklist.title: Falsify invariant: exit churn limits allow more validators to exit than permitted per epoch
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Simulate a fork transition with maximum active validator count. 2. Submit exit requests exceeding the computed churn limit per epoch. 3. Verify the protocol enforces the churn limit and queues excess exits. 4. Test edge case: exact churn limit boundary (N exits where N = limit). 5. Test with concurrent voluntary exits and forced exits (slashing) to verify combined limit enforcement.
executable_checks: unit_test: exit churn limit computation at fork transition
simulation: mass exit scenario
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-ELECTRA-INV-107. Primary element SPEC-ELECTRA. Invariant: attempt to bypass exit churn limits during fork transition.

checklist.title: Falsify assumption: validator set state is inconsistent at fork boundary
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Simulate an Electra fork transition with pending validator operations (activations, exits, slashings) at the fork boundary. 2. Check if any partially-applied state transitions exist after fork processing. 3. Verify all pending operations are either fully applied or fully deferred. 4. Test with a validator whose activation epoch equals the fork epoch. 5. Compare post-fork state across multiple client implementations.
executable_checks: simulation: fork transition with pending validator operations
cross_client_test: post-fork state consistency
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-ELECTRA-PRECOND-103. Assumption ASSUM-ELECTRA-FORK-02. Pre-condition: attempt to create inconsistent validator state at fork boundary.

checklist.title: Falsify invariant: withdrawal credentials change from 0x01 back to 0x00 is possible
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Process a BLS-to-execution change (0x00 -> 0x01) for a validator. 2. Attempt to submit another change operation reverting to 0x00 credentials. 3. Verify the protocol rejects the reversion. 4. Test via direct state manipulation in a test environment. 5. Verify no code path allows re-setting withdrawal credentials prefix to 0x00 after 0x01 is set.
executable_checks: unit_test: withdrawal credential irreversibility
state_test: direct state manipulation attempt
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-CAPELLA-VAL-INV-008. Primary element SPEC-CAPELLA-VAL. Invariant: attempt to reverse 0x01 credentials back to 0x00.

checklist.title: Falsify ambiguity resolution: enforcement mechanism for non-existent to existent-but-empty differs across clients
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Execute a transaction that would create an empty account (zero balance, zero nonce, no code). 2. Check if each client (Geth, Nethermind, Besu, Erigon) prevents this state transition. 3. Identify the specific enforcement mechanism in each client. 4. If mechanisms differ, test whether any sequence of operations exploits the difference to create divergent state. 5. Test with SELFDESTRUCT to empty account, CREATE2 to existing empty address.
executable_checks: cross_client_test: empty account creation prevention mechanism
state_test: non-existent to empty transition
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-EIP161-INV-111. Ambiguity AMB-EIP161-02. Invariant: attempt to show enforcement mechanisms diverge.

checklist.title: Falsify invariant: EIP-161 account deletion is applied during intermediate execution steps
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Create a transaction that touches an empty account mid-execution and then interacts with it again later. 2. Verify the account is still accessible during intermediate steps. 3. Verify deletion only occurs at transaction end. 4. Test with nested CALLs: inner call touches empty account, outer call reads it. 5. Compare intermediate state snapshots across clients.
executable_checks: state_test: empty account accessibility during tx execution
cross_client_test: deletion timing
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-EIP161-INV-119. Primary element SPEC-EIP161. Invariant: attempt to observe premature account deletion.

checklist.title: Falsify assumption: miner rewards or SUICIDE are not correctly identified as account touches
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Mine a block where coinbase is an empty account and verify it is touched (not deleted). 2. Execute SELFDESTRUCT sending value to an empty account and verify it is touched. 3. Execute SELFDESTRUCT sending zero value to an empty account and verify deletion behavior. 4. Test with uncle reward to empty coinbase. 5. Verify all touch scenarios consistently prevent incorrect deletion.
executable_checks: state_test: miner reward to empty coinbase
state_test: SELFDESTRUCT to empty account
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-EIP161-PRECOND-115. Assumption ASSUM-EIP161-03. Pre-condition: attempt to show miner rewards/SUICIDE are not counted as touches.

checklist.title: Falsify ambiguity resolution: merkle branch at/exceeding Electra depth is handled differently across clients
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Construct a LightClientStore with merkle branches already at or exceeding the required Electra depth. 2. Apply the Electra fork upgrade function. 3. Verify behavior: are branches truncated, left unchanged, or does an error occur? 4. Compare across light client implementations. 5. If behavior differs, document the divergence.
executable_checks: unit_test: merkle branch upgrade with pre-existing sufficient depth
cross_client_test: upgrade behavior
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-ELECTRA-LC-FORK-INV-012. Ambiguity AMB-ELECTRA-LC-FORK-02. Invariant: attempt to show divergent handling of already-deep branches.

checklist.title: Falsify post-condition: upgraded LightClientStore has incorrect merkle branch depth
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Create a pre-Electra LightClientStore with known merkle branch depths. 2. Apply the Electra upgrade function. 3. Verify every merkle branch has the correct depth for the new SSZ structure. 4. Test with branches of various pre-upgrade depths (minimum, typical, maximum). 5. Verify upgraded branches can successfully prove inclusion against post-Electra state roots.
executable_checks: unit_test: merkle branch depth after Electra upgrade
integration_test: inclusion proof verification post-upgrade
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-ELECTRA-LC-FORK-POSTCOND-016. Primary element SPEC-ELECTRA-LC-FORK. Post-condition: attempt to find incorrect depth after upgrade.

checklist.title: Falsify ambiguity resolution: unknown identity scheme handling differs across clients
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Create an ENR record with a non-standard identity scheme (e.g., 'v5'). 2. Present this ENR to multiple client implementations. 3. Check whether each client rejects, ignores, or attempts to process the record. 4. If behavior differs, assess impact on peer discovery. 5. Test with completely unknown scheme name.
executable_checks: integration_test: ENR with unknown identity scheme across clients
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-EIP778-INV-020. Ambiguity AMB-EIP778-01. Invariant: attempt to show divergent behavior for unknown identity schemes.

checklist.title: Falsify invariant: ENR record exceeds 300-byte RLP size limit
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Construct an ENR with the maximum number of key-value pairs approaching 300 bytes. 2. Add one more key-value pair to exceed 300 bytes. 3. Attempt to publish and propagate the oversized ENR. 4. Verify all clients reject ENRs exceeding 300 bytes. 5. Test at exactly 300 bytes and 301 bytes.
executable_checks: unit_test: ENR size limit enforcement at 300 bytes
integration_test: oversized ENR propagation rejection
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-EIP778-INV-028. Primary element SPEC-EIP778. Invariant: attempt to create and propagate an oversized ENR.

checklist.title: Falsify assumption: private key recovery from ENR public key or signatures is feasible
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Verify the ENR uses secp256k1 for the 'v4' identity scheme. 2. Confirm key derivation follows standard ECDSA with adequate key length. 3. Check if multiple ENR signatures from the same key leak information (nonce reuse). 4. Verify signature generation uses RFC 6979 deterministic nonces. 5. Assess theoretical attack cost given current computational capabilities.
executable_checks: cryptographic_analysis: ENR signature nonce reuse check
static_analysis: signature generation method
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-EIP778-PRECOND-024. Assumption ASSUM-EIP778-02. Pre-condition: attempt to show private key recovery is feasible.

checklist.title: Falsify ambiguity resolution: max uint64 fork epoch causes implementation-specific behavior
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Set EIP7805_FORK_EPOCH to uint64 max (18446744073709551615) in a test environment. 2. Verify this effectively means 'not yet scheduled' across all clients. 3. Check if any client performs arithmetic on this value that could overflow. 4. Test epoch comparison logic with this sentinel value. 5. Verify no client accidentally activates the fork due to integer overflow in epoch calculations.
executable_checks: unit_test: fork epoch comparison with uint64 max
cross_client_test: sentinel value handling
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-EIP7805-INV-032. Ambiguity AMB-EIP7805-02. Invariant: attempt to show uint64 max sentinel causes unexpected behavior.

checklist.title: Falsify invariant: EIP7805_FORK_VERSION collides with an existing fork version
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Enumerate all defined fork versions across mainnet, testnets, and devnets. 2. Compare EIP7805_FORK_VERSION against the full list. 3. Verify uniqueness. 4. Check if any test configuration accidentally reuses the version. 5. Verify fork version is checked during domain computation for signatures.
executable_checks: static_analysis: fork version uniqueness across all networks
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-EIP7805-INV-036. Primary element SPEC-EIP7805. Invariant: attempt to find a fork version collision.

checklist.title: Falsify ambiguity resolution: MAX_BLOB_GAS_PER_BLOCK to blob count relationship is interpreted differently
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Calculate the implied maximum blob count from MAX_BLOB_GAS_PER_BLOCK and GAS_PER_BLOB. 2. Compare this calculation across client implementations. 3. Test with a block containing the maximum number of blobs. 4. Test with one blob over the implied maximum. 5. Verify all clients agree on the exact maximum blob count.
executable_checks: cross_client_test: maximum blob count derivation from gas parameters
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-EIP7872-INV-040. Ambiguity AMB-EIP7872-02. Invariant: attempt to show clients derive different max blob counts.

checklist.title: Falsify pre-condition: USER_CONFIGURED_MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK accepts invalid values
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Set USER_CONFIGURED_MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK to 0 and verify rejection or safe handling. 2. Set to a negative value (if type allows) and verify rejection. 3. Set to a value exceeding the protocol maximum and verify it is capped or rejected. 4. Set to the exact protocol maximum and verify acceptance. 5. Test with non-integer values if the configuration interface allows.
executable_checks: unit_test: USER_CONFIGURED_MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK validation bounds
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-EIP7872-PRECOND-044. Primary element SPEC-EIP7872. Pre-condition: attempt to set invalid blob count configuration.

checklist.title: Falsify invariant: extended stack access opcode does not trigger exceptional failure for out-of-bounds operand
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Execute extended stack access opcodes with operands referencing depth 0 (top of stack) and verify success. 2. Execute with operand referencing exactly current stack depth and verify exceptional failure. 3. Execute with operand = current stack depth - 1 (last valid) and verify success. 4. Test with maximum possible stack depth. 5. Verify gas is consumed correctly on exceptional failure.
executable_checks: unit_test: extended stack opcode bounds checking
state_test: stack depth boundary conditions
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-EIP8024-INV-079. Primary element SPEC-EIP8024. Invariant: attempt to access beyond stack depth without failure.

checklist.title: Falsify assumption: static analysis tools cannot accurately track stack state with extended depth operations
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Write Solidity/Yul contracts using extended stack access patterns. 2. Run through major static analysis tools (Slither, Mythril, Securify). 3. Check if the tools correctly model the stack state with extended depth operations. 4. Identify any false positives or false negatives caused by the new opcodes. 5. Test with deeply nested stack manipulation patterns.
executable_checks: manual_review: static analysis tool compatibility with EIP-8024 opcodes
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-EIP8024-PRECOND-075. Assumption ASSUM-EIP8024-02. Pre-condition: attempt to show static analysis breaks with extended stack.

checklist.title: Falsify ambiguity resolution: TLOAD of unwritten key returns different values across clients
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Execute TLOAD for a key that was never written in the current transaction. 2. Verify the return value is 0 (expected default). 3. Test across multiple clients (Geth, Nethermind, Besu, Erigon). 4. Test TLOAD after TSTORE(key, 0) vs never-written key to verify identical behavior. 5. If any client returns a non-zero default, document the divergence.
executable_checks: cross_client_test: TLOAD default value for unwritten keys
unit_test: TLOAD vs TSTORE(0) equivalence
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-PRAGUE-STORAGE-INV-052. Ambiguity AMB-PRAGUE-STORAGE-02. Invariant: attempt to show clients return different defaults.

checklist.title: Falsify assumption: static context flag can be manipulated through external means
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Enter a STATICCALL context and verify the static flag is set. 2. Within STATICCALL, attempt DELEGATECALL to a contract that tries to clear the static flag. 3. Attempt to use assembly/low-level tricks to modify the EVM execution context. 4. Test if any precompile call can alter the static context. 5. Verify the flag persists correctly through all nested call types.
executable_checks: unit_test: static flag persistence through nested calls
state_test: DELEGATECALL within STATICCALL
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-PRAGUE-STORAGE-PRECOND-056. Assumption ASSUM-PRAGUE-STORAGE-03. Pre-condition: attempt to manipulate static context flag externally.

checklist.title: Falsify pre-condition: SSTORE in STATICCALL context does not revert
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Enter STATICCALL context and attempt SSTORE. 2. Verify the operation reverts with the correct error. 3. Test TSTORE in STATICCALL context (should also revert per EIP-1153 semantics). 4. Test SSTORE via DELEGATECALL within STATICCALL. 5. Verify gas is consumed correctly on revert. 6. Test that no state change persists after the revert.
executable_checks: unit_test: SSTORE revert in STATICCALL
state_test: TSTORE in STATICCALL
state_test: DELEGATECALL+SSTORE in STATICCALL
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-PRAGUE-STORAGE-PRECOND-060. Primary element SPEC-PRAGUE-STORAGE. Pre-condition: attempt to write storage from static context.
